warning: A registry entry identifies a candidate Practice target; it does not establish that a question correctly assesses this exact publisher lesson, that a generator renders, that grading is secure, or that attempts are persisted. These remain unverified for ALL 131 lessons.

rows.title: Moving in the Plane
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s describe ways figures can move in the plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Partner investigation: each learner secretly draws a starting and ending position of the same triangular card, then gives verbal directions for the other to reconstruct the move. Test the explanation on an asymmetric figure; a vague instruction such as “move it over there” cannot be reproduced uniquely.

rows.title: Naming the Moves
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s be more precise about describing moves of figures in the plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Make three original paper examples with an asymmetric quadrilateral. Slide one tracing, turn a second around a chosen corner and flip a third over a drawn line. Sort the three pairs by the evidence you can show; do not infer “rotation” merely because the figures have moved.

rows.title: Grid Moves
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s transform some figures on grids.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Student task: draw an irregular polygon and its translated image on a square grid, then choose a center and draw a turned copy on an isometric grid. Compare all corresponding vertices. Drawings and open construction explanations need accessible graphical/teacher review; three numerical coordinate examples alone cannot establish complete student assessment.

rows.title: Making the Moves
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s draw and describe translations, rotations, and reflections.

rows.title: Coordinate Moves
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s transform some figures and see what happens to the coordinates of points.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Original task: a student supplies an incorrect image coordinate after a move. Diagnose the error using point-to-point distances or the required center/line. A teacher checks the explanation; numeric pairs can be independently checked.

rows.title: Describing Transformations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s transform some polygons in the coordinate plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: An original Edulytiks investigation uses triangle A(1,1), B(3,1), C(1,2). First translate by (2,0), then reflect across the y-axis. Draw each intermediate image and name the ordered steps. Ask whether reversing the order would produce the same result.

rows.title: No Bending or Stretching
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s compare measurements before and after translations, rotations, and reflections.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a triangle with vertices (1,1),(4,1),(1,5). Its legs have lengths 3 and 4 and its third side has length 5. Reflect it across the y-axis. Use a ruler and the Pythagorean relation to show that the image retains the same three lengths.

rows.title: Rotation Patterns
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s rotate figures in a plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Make a first-party geometric rosette using a simple L-shaped figure traced around a chosen point. Label each rotated image and state the generating angle. A teacher assesses drawing accuracy, repeated figures and explanation; do not claim the rosette itself is machine-graded.

rows.title: Moves in Parallel
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s transform some lines.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw horizontal lines y=1 and y=4, then translate both upward two units. Compare their separation and slopes. Next rotate a pair of horizontal line segments a quarter-turn about the origin and observe how their directions change together.

rows.title: Composing Figures
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use reasoning about rigid transformations to find measurements without measuring.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Original task: build a 6-by-2 rectangle from two identical 3-by-2 rectangles. Translate one piece next to the other and ask what happens to the shared interior boundary. Discuss which lengths become exterior edges.

rows.title: What Is the Same?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s decide whether shapes are the same.

rows.title: Congruent Polygons
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s decide if two figures are congruent.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw quadrilateral A(1,1), B(4,1), C(4,3), D(1,3) and translate it by (−5,2). Label A′,B′,C′,D′. Check that all four sides and right angles correspond.

rows.title: Congruence
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find ways to test congruence of interesting figures.

rows.title: Alternate Interior Angles
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore why some angles are always equal.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw two parallel horizontal lines and one slanted transversal. The interior angles lie between the two lines. Alternate interior angles are on opposite sides of the transversal; they can be matched by an appropriate 180° turn around the midpoint between intersection points.

rows.title: Adding the Angles in a Triangle
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore angles in triangles.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a scalene triangle, cut out the three corners and assemble them at a point so that the three wedges form a straight angle. This supports the fact that the angles in any Euclidean triangle add to 180°.

rows.title: Parallel Lines and the Angles in a Triangle
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s see why the angles in a triangle add to 180 degrees.

rows.title: Rotate and Tessellate
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's make complex patterns using transformations.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a triangle tile and make repeated rotated or translated copies on an accessible grid. Explain why the boundaries meet without gaps and why the transformations preserve tile shape.

rows.title: Projecting and Scaling
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore scaling.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw center O, triangle A,B,C and image A′,B′,C′ along the same rays from O. Estimate a common ratio OA′/OA for all three corners. A teacher checks the source-specific projection diagram and proportional reasoning; numeric scale ratios alone do not verify drawing quality.

rows.title: Circular Grid
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s dilate figures on circular grids.

rows.title: Dilations with no Grid
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s dilate figures not on grids.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Mark an arbitrary center O and a triangle ABC. Draw rays OA, OB, OC; along each ray mark A′,B′,C′ with OA′=k·OA and so on. Join image vertices in the original order.

rows.title: Dilations on a Square Grid
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s dilate figures on a square grid.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a triangle on grid paper and dilate it from O by factor 2, then repeat with a different center. Explain why the second image is placed differently. The drawing and explanation require human review.

rows.title: More Dilations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s look at dilations in the coordinate plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate a coordinate rectangle of side lengths 2 and 3 at different positive factors. Record old and new side lengths and compare the area ratio. Written justification about why area scales by the square needs teacher scoring.

rows.title: Similarity
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore similar figures.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a 3-by-5 rectangle and a 6-by-10 rectangle. Determine the common scale factor. Compare with a 6-by-9 rectangle and explain why one uniform dilation cannot map the first to the second.

rows.title: Similar Polygons
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s look at sides and angles of similar polygons.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate two quadrilaterals with one matching angle but inconsistent side ratios. Explain why a single angle is insufficient. Diagram correspondence and explanatory reasoning are teacher-scored.

rows.title: Similar Triangles
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s look at similar triangles.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw two triangles with angles 40°,60°,80°. Give them different side lengths but the same proportional ratios. Check that a rotation or reflection may be needed before a dilation aligns them.

rows.title: Side Length Quotients in Similar Triangles
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find missing side lengths in triangles.

rows.title: Meet Slope
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s learn about the slope of a line.

rows.title: Writing Equations for Lines
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore the relationship between points on a line and the slope of the line.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a line through points (1,3) and (3,7), calculate slope and write the equation. The teacher reviews the plotted graph and intercept interpretation; numerical substitutions can be machine-checked.

rows.title: Using Equations for Lines
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s write equations for lines.

rows.title: The Shadow Knows
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use shadows to find the heights of an object.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate an original Edulytiks scenario: a 1.5-meter vertical pole casts a 2-meter shadow and a tree casts a 10-meter shadow at the same time. Draw and label both triangles, solve the tree height, then discuss how uneven ground or moving sunlight could invalidate the model.

rows.title: Understanding Proportional Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s study some graphs.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate a chart of notebooks at $3 each: points (0,0), (1,3), (2,6). Draw axes labeled notebooks and cost, explain the meaning of the origin, and distinguish a line with a fixed admission fee. A teacher checks explanations and accurate graph labeling.

rows.title: Graphs of Proportional Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's think about scale.

rows.title: Representing Proportional Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's graph proportional relationships.

rows.title: Comparing Proportional Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s compare proportional relationships.

rows.title: Introduction to Linear Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore some relationships between two variables.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate a bike-rental fee: $4 booking charge plus $3 per hour. Make a table, graph and explain the intercept. The teacher reviews the interpretation; numbers alone do not verify the story.

rows.title: More Linear Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore some more relationships between two variables.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Analyze a tank with 18 liters losing 3 liters each minute. Build a table until empty, discuss the limited physical domain, and distinguish that from purely algebraic continuation. Teacher review checks model assumptions.

rows.title: Representations of Linear Relationships
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s write equations from real situations.

rows.title: Translating to $y=mx+b$
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s see what happens to the equations of translated lines.

rows.title: Slopes Don't Have to be Positive
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find out what a negative slope means.

rows.title: Calculating Slope
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s calculate slope from two points.

rows.title: Equations of All Kinds of Lines
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s write equations for vertical and horizontal lines.

rows.title: Solutions to Linear Equations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s think about what it means to be a solution to a linear equation with two variables in it.

rows.title: More Solutions to Linear Equations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find solutions to more linear equations.

rows.title: Using Linear Relations to Solve Problems
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s write equations for real-world situations and think about their solutions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Original Edulytiks task: a repair shop charges $18 inspection plus $7 per labor hour. Write total cost, solve when a bill is $60, and explain why the time cannot be negative. A teacher evaluates variable definitions and contextual interpretation.

rows.title: Number Puzzles
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s solve some puzzles!

rows.title: Keeping the Equation Balanced
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's figure out unknown weights on balanced hangers.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Make an original picture with two identical bags and a three-unit weight balancing an eleven-unit weight. Interpret it as 2x+3=11. A teacher evaluates diagram alignment and explanation; one numerical result does not verify the physical model.

rows.title: Balanced Moves
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's rewrite equations while keeping the same solutions.

rows.title: More Balanced Moves
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's rewrite some more equations while keeping the same solutions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct a diagram showing equal expressions 5x+2 and 2x+14. Explain how removing two x-tiles from both sides isolates the remaining three. A teacher reviews the algebraic diagram and validity of each step.

rows.title: Solving Any Linear Equation
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's solve linear equations.

rows.title: Strategic Solving
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's solve linear equations like a boss.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Give students 4(x+3)=28 and ask them to solve in two ways, explain what is more economical, and critique a common distribution mistake. Teacher evaluation focuses on mathematical explanation rather than speed alone.

rows.title: All, Some, or No Solutions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s think about how many solutions an equation can have.

rows.title: How Many Solutions?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s solve equations with different numbers of solutions.

rows.title: When Are They the Same?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use equations to think about situations.

rows.title: On or Off the Line?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s interpret the meaning of points in a coordinate plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate a taxi fare F=4+2d. Sort points (0,4), (3,10), (3,11) by substitution and explain which are valid fare-distance combinations. A teacher checks graph reading and context.

rows.title: On Both of the Lines
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use lines to think about situations.

rows.title: Systems of Equations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s learn what a system of equations is.

rows.title: Solving Systems of Equations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s solve systems of equations.

rows.title: Solving More Systems
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s solve systems of equations.

rows.title: Writing Systems of Equations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s write systems of equations from real-world situations.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Invent a ticket scenario with adult tickets $8, child tickets $5, 10 tickets total and $65 total revenue. Write two equations and discuss physical restrictions to nonnegative integers. Teacher review is needed for variable definitions and consistency of the story.

rows.title: Solving Problems with Systems of Equations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's solve some gnarly problems.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Consider a mixture of apples and pears: eight fruits total, apples $2 each, pears $3 each, total cost $19. Determine both counts and explain why each condition matters. Teacher review checks context and reasoning.

rows.title: Inputs and Outputs
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s make some rules.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Partner task: describe a hidden rule using three input-output pairs and ask a peer to predict two more. Multiple rules may fit only three examples, so give additional evidence rather than pretending the pattern is uniquely determined. Teacher review examines rule clarity.

rows.title: Introduction to Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s learn what a function is.

rows.title: Equations for Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find outputs from equations.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Compare f(x)=2x−5 and g(x)=x² with positive and negative inputs. Teacher review checks clear notation and explanation of why inverse output questions may have multiple answers.

rows.title: Tables, Equations, and Graphs of Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s connect equations and graphs of functions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Plot the square rule with labeled axes, join points smoothly based on the real domain, and distinguish the exact equation from sparse observations. Teacher review checks axes and the curve.

rows.title: More Graphs of Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s interpret graphs of functions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Compare a journey: start at 0 km, reach 6 km at 2 hours, stay until 3 hours, then return to 0 km by 5 hours. Teacher reviews the graph and story correspondence.

rows.title: Even More Graphs of Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s draw a graph from a story.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw an original tank-fill story: 0 L at minute 0, 12 L at minute 3, a pause to minute 5, then 20 L at minute 7. Explain the graph segments and why a teacher must evaluate the written interpretation.

rows.title: Connecting Representations of Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s connect tables, equations, graphs, and stories of functions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Compare the plotted points with a continuous line and explain why fractional tickets are not physically meaningful. Teacher review checks the correspondence and restrictions.

rows.title: Linear Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s investigate linear functions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Compare two input-output tables: f(x)=3x+2 and g(x)=x². Write evidence based on differences. Teacher reviews the explanation and the selected representative points.

rows.title: Linear Models
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s model situations with linear functions.

rows.title: Piecewise Linear Functions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore functions built out of linear pieces.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Model a parking fee: $3 for up to one hour, then $3 plus $2 per additional whole hour. Compare with a continuous piecewise rule if fractional hours are permitted. Teacher review checks the selected billing policy and graph step/segment choice.

rows.title: Filling Containers
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s fill containers with water.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Original comparison: pour equal 100-mL portions into a tall narrow rectangular container and a wider one. Record water heights and discuss where a linear graph is justified. Teacher-scored diagrams and observations matter; predictions cannot replace actual measurements.

rows.title: How Much Will Fit?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s reason about the volume of different shapes.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct two small paper containers with the same height but different bases. Predict capacities first and then verify with unit cubes or water where safe. Teacher review assesses the physical representation.

rows.title: The Volume of a Cylinder
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore cylinders and their volumes.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct an original paper cylinder with marked radius and height and discuss the relationship between a circle drawing and a 3D solid. A teacher checks labeling and reasoning; numeric formula substitution is a separate graded task.

rows.title: Finding Cylinder Dimensions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s figure out the dimensions of cylinders.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Use a first-party container-design task in which a required capacity and fixed radius determine height. Explain how a change in diameter affects required height. Teacher-scored diagrams complement numerical algebra.

rows.title: The Volume of a Cone
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore cones and their volumes.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a cone and its circumscribing cylinder, mark the same vertical height, and compare capacity through an original measure-and-pour investigation. Teacher assessment checks visual reasoning; formula calculations alone do not prove construction parity.

rows.title: Finding Cone Dimensions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s figure out the dimensions of cones.

rows.title: Scaling One Dimension
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s see how changing one dimension changes the volume of a shape.

rows.title: Scaling Two Dimensions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s change more dimensions of shapes.

rows.title: Estimating a Hemisphere
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s estimate volume of hemispheres with figures we know.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a hemisphere of radius 3 fitting inside a cylinder with radius 3 and height 3. Estimate an upper bound of 27π cm³, then discuss that the exact hemisphere volume is 18π cm³. A teacher checks the conceptual diagram and assumptions.

rows.title: The Volume of a Sphere
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore spheres and their volumes.

rows.title: Cylinders, Cones, and Spheres
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find the volume of shapes.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Create a labeled table with one solid of each type, compute volumes and justify the formula selected. Teacher review checks diagrams, units and how the chosen measurements correspond to each solid.

rows.title: Volume As a Function of . . .
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s compare water heights in different containers.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Sketch volume-height graphs for a cylinder and an upright cone with the same total height. Explain why equal height increments need different volume increments in the cone. Teacher review is essential for diagram orientation, modeling assumptions and graph shape.

rows.title: Organizing Data
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find ways to show patterns in data
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Student task: choose axes and plot the five measurement pairs, then compare a two-variable scatter plot to separate unpaired summaries. A teacher checks axis units, retained pairings, and written reasoning; no automated correctness claim for self-collected data.

rows.title: Plotting Data
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s collect and display some data about the class.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw an original scatter plot with both axes measured in centimeters, appropriate scales, and no connecting line through separate pupils. If a student gathers real observations, the teacher reviews ethical data collection and accurate plotted pairs; do not submit personal class data to external services.

rows.title: What a Point in a Scatter Plot Means
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s investigate points in scatter plots.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Using fictional paired data (1,3),(2,5),(3,7),(4,9),(5,4), identify the dot that differs most from an upward linear pattern and explain what additional information should be checked. Teacher-scored reasoning addresses measurement uncertainty.

rows.title: Fitting a Line to Data
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s look at the scatter plots as a whole.

rows.title: Describing Trends in Scatter Plots
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s look for associations between variables.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Sort original fictional patterns: (1,8),(2,6),(3,4),(4,2) has strong downward trend; (1,3),(2,7),(3,2),(4,8) has no obvious simple trend. Teacher review checks explanations and uncertainty.

rows.title: The Slope of a Fitted Line
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's look at how changing one variable changes another.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Use a fictional line through (1,54) and (4,66). Compute slope and intercept and discuss uncertainty from scatter. Teacher review assesses contextual language and limitations.

rows.title: Observing More Patterns in Scatter Plots
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's look for other patterns in data.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Graph original points (−2,4),(−1,1),(0,0),(1,1),(2,4). Explain why they form a curved pattern and why a straight line would miss their structure. Teacher feedback checks the sketch and reasoning.

rows.title: Analyzing Bivariate Data
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s analyze data like a pro.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Investigate five original points (1,3),(2,4),(3,7),(4,8),(5,9). Compute how y generally changes and identify that one rise is larger than others. A teacher reviews statistical explanation, not a single predetermined adjective.

rows.title: Looking for Associations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s look for associations in data.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Original fictional table: Group A 12 choose bus, 8 walk; Group B 5 choose bus, 15 walk. Compute within-group proportions. Teacher review checks fairness of comparison and causal caution.

rows.title: Using Data Displays to Find Associations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use data displays to find associations.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Use an original table: A 30 choose fruit and 10 choose cereal; B 12 choose fruit and 28 choose cereal. Predict each bar segment and compare. Teacher review assesses correctly labeled percent axes and context.

rows.title: Gone In 30 Seconds
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s gather and analyze some timing data.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Use fictional counts (10,12),(15,17),(20,21),(25,24) for worked analysis. Teachers review ethical collection, the scatter plot, and whether conclusions are appropriately qualified. One numerical rate cannot certify experimental design.

rows.title: Exponent Review
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s review exponents.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Represent powers using original square/cube diagrams and repeated-product notation. Teacher review checks whether the visual model correctly distinguishes base and exponent.

rows.title: Multiplying Powers of Ten
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore patterns with exponents when we multiply powers of 10.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a place-value table for 10²×10³ and explain why the outcome is 10⁵. A teacher checks mathematical pattern reasoning and table alignment.

rows.title: Powers of Powers of 10
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's look at powers of powers of 10.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Make an original exponent-tree representation grouping factors into equal blocks. Teacher review checks the explanation of grouping versus product.

rows.title: Dividing Powers of 10
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore patterns with exponents when we divide powers of 10.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw factor-cancellation rows to explain 10⁵/10², then explore 10²/10⁵. A teacher assesses the cancellation model, while exact numeric answers are independently checkable.

rows.title: Negative Exponents with Powers of 10
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s see what happens when exponents are negative.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct a place-value number line from 1 to 0.001 with labels. Teacher checks ordered spacing and explanation; a numerical conversion alone does not validate the drawn model.

rows.title: What about Other Bases?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore exponent patterns with bases other than 10.

rows.title: Practice with Rational Bases
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's practice with exponents.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Create a rational-base card sort showing two expressions with the same value, then justify without floating-point rounding. Teacher checks symbolic reasoning and equivalence.

rows.title: Combining Bases
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s multiply expressions with different bases.

rows.title: Describing Large and Small Numbers Using Powers of 10
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find out how to use powers of 10 to write large or small numbers.

rows.title: Representing Large Numbers on the Number Line
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s visualize large numbers on the number line using powers of 10.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a line from 0 to 5,000,000 with million-unit spacing; locate 2.5×10⁶ and explain its midpoint position. A teacher checks the scale and labeling.

rows.title: Representing Small Numbers on the Number Line
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s visualize small numbers on the number line using powers of 10.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Create an original micro-distance axis and compare 0.0002,0.0005 and 0.0008. Teacher review checks the precision and regular spacing.

rows.title: Applications of Arithmetic with Powers of 10
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let's use powers of 10 to help us make calculations with large and small numbers.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Model the area of a microsensor rectangle of dimensions 3×10⁻³ m and 2×10⁻² m; find area and explain why the product exponent is −5. Teacher checks dimensional interpretation.

rows.title: Definition of Scientific Notation
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use scientific notation to describe large and small numbers.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Write measurements from an original chart into normalized notation. Teacher checks decimal-place reasoning and units, not just pattern memorization.

rows.title: Multiplying, Dividing, and Estimating with Scientific Notation
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s multiply and divide with scientific notation to answer questions about animals, careers, and planets.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Compare original contexts of microscopic cell length and astronomical distance without claiming the same measurement units. Teacher reviews the interpretation and order-of-magnitude estimate.

rows.title: Adding and Subtracting with Scientific Notation
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s add and subtract using scientific notation to answer questions about animals and the solar system.

rows.title: Is a Smartphone Smart Enough to Go to the Moon?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s compare digital media and computer hardware using scientific notation.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Original hypothetical scenario: device A stores 1.2×10¹¹ bytes, device B stores 3×10¹⁰ bytes. Compare capacity and express device A in bits. Teacher reviews modeling limitations, evidence sources and why capacity alone does not establish flight suitability.

rows.title: The Areas of Squares and Their Side Lengths
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s investigate the squares and their side lengths.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct paper square tiles with side lengths 1,2,3,4 and compare the number of unit-square tiles. The relationship A=s² means a square with area 25 has side length 5 units, not ±5, because physical lengths are nonnegative.

rows.title: Side Lengths and Areas
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s investigate some more squares.

rows.title: Rational and Irrational Numbers
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s learn about irrational numbers.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct a number-card sort using 1/2, √4, √2, 0.125, 0.333… and π. A teacher checks explanations and exact classifications rather than approximated display strings.

rows.title: Square Roots on the Number Line
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore square roots.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Sketch and annotate the construction rather than only writing 1.414. Teacher evaluation is necessary for a valid geometric placement and scale.

rows.title: Reasoning About Square Roots
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s approximate square roots.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Make an original table of nearby squares to locate √30 and √50. A teacher reviews estimation and why a proposed bound is mathematically valid.

rows.title: Finding Side Lengths of Triangles
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find triangle side lengths.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw a 3-by-4 rectangle corner and connect endpoints to construct the right-triangle diagonal. Teacher review checks perpendicularity and correct side labels.

rows.title: A Proof of the Pythagorean Theorem
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s prove the Pythagorean Theorem.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Create a first-party paper-piece rearrangement with four labeled triangles, explain why the center is a square, and account for all pieces. Teacher review of construction and proof is required; a numeric exercise alone does not certify proof understanding.

rows.title: Finding Unknown Side Lengths
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find missing side lengths of right triangles.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Model a ladder as a right-triangle hypotenuse and its wall distance as a leg. Teacher reviews realism of perpendicular assumptions and units.

rows.title: The Converse
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s figure out if a triangle is a right triangle.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Sort independently prepared side triples into right and non-right groups with exact squared sums. Teacher checks the logical converse and classification.

rows.title: Applications of the Pythagorean Theorem
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore some applications of the Pythagorean Theorem.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw an original map with scale, perpendicular axes and a destination. Explain when right-angle assumptions are justified. Teacher checks the diagram and real-world interpretation.

rows.title: Finding Distances in the Coordinate Plane
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s find distances in the coordinate plane.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Plot a pair of points with negative coordinates, draw its right-triangle legs, and explain why differences rather than raw coordinates enter the formula. Teacher checks the constructed visual.

rows.title: Edge Lengths and Volumes
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore the relationship between volume and edge lengths of cubes.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Build 2×2×2 and 3×3×3 cube arrays from unit cubes or sketches, and explain why their volumes are 8 and 27. Teacher review of counting layers is required.

rows.title: Cube Roots
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s compare cube roots.

rows.title: Decimal Representations of Rational Numbers
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s learn more about how rational numbers can be represented.

rows.title: Infinite Decimal Expansions
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s think about infinite decimals.

rows.title: When Is the Same Size Not the Same Size?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s figure out how aspect ratio affects screen area.

rows.title: Tessellations of the Plane
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s explore geometric patterns!
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw an original irregular quadrilateral on squared paper, make rotated and translated copies, and test edge-to-edge fit. A teacher evaluates whether the actual drawing covers the selected region without gaps or overlaps, not just arithmetic.

rows.title: Regular Tessellations
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s make some regular tessellations.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Construct original samples from paper or a grid. Test hexagonal honeycomb and explain why three 120° corners close. Teacher review assesses regularity, edge matching and explanation.

rows.title: Tessellating Polygons
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s make tessellations with different polygons.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Make an original triangle tile with unequal sides and demonstrate a paired copy. Ask a partner to explain how translated parallelograms extend the pattern. Teacher review assesses the actual edge-matching diagram and reasoning.

rows.title: What Influences Temperature?
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s see if we can predict the weather.

rows.title: Plotting the Weather
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s construct a model.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Draw the points and fitted line with labeled units. Compare residuals at each observation and explain why the line is not a universal physical law. A teacher reviews graph quality and justification.

rows.title: Using and Interpreting a Mathematical Model
rows.teacherSourceGoal: Let’s use a model to make some predictions.
rows.originalTaskCandidateDescription: Student task: use a fictional fitted model to predict temperatures at two unmeasured latitudes and defend whether the model can support the inference. A teacher checks argumentation, context, extrapolation, units and the model’s limitations, not just numeric predictions.
